raw_response:
I farm a fairly big area now, but I’ve only done this for 3 years, so I don’t want to gamble too much. I’ll still keep wheat-maize as the main system on 220 mu because it is the steadiest here in Quzhou and I know how to manage it. The other 120.1 mu I’ll split between soybean and oilseed so I’m not putting everything into one price and one weather risk. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I’ll save irrigation for the key stages instead of watering too often. On fertilizer, I won’t chase the highest rate. I’ll use enough to hold yield, split the nitrogen on wheat and maize, and keep some cash in hand in case the season turns dry or pest pressure gets worse. Since there are only 4 people in my household and 340.1 mu is too much for family labor alone, I’ll use machinery and hire people at the busy times.
